questions.q: What does reclassifying an asset change?
options: Its category, with cost and usually location unchanged
questions.explain: Reclassification corrects which category an asset belongs to, without changing its cost or (usually) its location.

questions.q: Why can reclassification trigger catch-up depreciation even though nothing about the physical asset changed?
options: Because category books carry default depreciation method and life, so a category change can alter the depreciation calculation
Because reclassification always changes the asset's cost automatically
Because reclassification requires the asset to be retired first
Because Oracle Fusion Assets recalculates randomly on any transaction
questions.explain: Since category books set default depreciation rules, moving an asset to a category with a different life or method changes its depreciation calculation going forward, which can produce a catch-up gap.

questions.q: A $40,000 asset moves from a 10-year category ($3,200 depreciation over 2 years already taken) to a 5-year category that should have taken $16,000 over those same 2 years. What is the catch-up amount?
questions.explain: $16,000 (what should have been taken under the new category) minus $6,400 (what was actually taken) equals a $9,600 catch-up.

questions.q: Which transaction is the correct one when an asset's dollar amount, not its category or location, is wrong?
questions.explain: A cost adjustment is the correct transaction when the recorded dollar amount needs correction, as opposed to category (reclassification) or location (transfer).

questions.q: Can an asset need both a reclassification and a transfer over its lifetime?
options: No, only one correction type can ever be applied to an asset
Yes, each is a distinct transaction and both can be applied in sequence
No, reclassification automatically includes a transfer
Yes, but only if the asset is also retired first
questions.explain: Reclassification and transfer are distinct transactions answering distinct questions, and an asset's transaction history can include both over time.
